subject.title: Feature: a registerable, authoritative approval-resolver seam (capability-level, cross-harness, exclusive) for external approval providers

question: Should OpenClaw introduce an authoritative, exclusive external approval-resolver security boundary across native, Codex, ACP, and delegated execution paths, or keep external providers limited to the existing plugin-owned approval model?
rationale: This chooses a permanent authorization and plugin API contract, including which effects must be covered and whether existing operator approval surfaces may be suppressed; source-level implementation mechanics cannot safely decide that policy.

options.title: Commission a narrow security RFC
options.body: Define capability coverage, resolver precedence, request/proof binding, failure semantics, persistence, and cross-harness conformance tests before exposing a generic plugin seam.

options.title: Retain plugin-owned approvals only
options.body: Document that external providers may gate only the existing plugin-hook approval path and cannot claim authoritative coverage for native or ACP execution.

options.title: Split the work by harness
options.body: Approve a bounded first slice for one execution harness only, with an explicit statement that it is not an authoritative cross-harness security guarantee.

recommendation.title: Commission a narrow security RFC
recommendation.body: Define capability coverage, resolver precedence, request/proof binding, failure semantics, persistence, and cross-harness conformance tests before exposing a generic plugin seam.

likelyOwner.reason: They own the closest active public proposal for external plugin approval APIs and can help distinguish a narrow approval extension from the new authoritative security boundary requested here.
